------------------------------ MODULE W4Od4m1p4t2 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Stations, Lines, Bays, MaxWait

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES tokenAt, stage, held, waiting, pool
vars == <<tokenAt, stage, held, waiting, pool>>

RingNext(s) == (s % Stations) + 1
LineOf(s) == IF s % 2 = 1 THEN "L1" ELSE "L2"

Occupied == {s \in 1 .. Stations : stage[s] # "free"}
UsedBays == {held[s] : s \in Occupied}

Init ==
    /\ tokenAt = 1
    /\ stage = [s \in 1 .. Stations |-> "free"]
    /\ held = [s \in 1 .. Stations |-> NONE]
    /\ waiting = [l \in Lines |-> 0]
    /\ pool = Bays

Arrive(l) ==
    /\ waiting[l] < MaxWait
    /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![l] = waiting[l] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, stage, held, pool>>

PassToken(s) ==
    /\ tokenAt = s
    /\ tokenAt' = RingNext(s)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, held, waiting, pool>>

Admit(s) ==
    /\ tokenAt = s
    /\ stage[s] = "free"
    /\ waiting[LineOf(s)] > 0
    /\ pool # {}
    /\ \E b \in pool :
        /\ pool' = pool \ {b}
        /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![s] = b]
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "washing"]
    /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![LineOf(s)] = waiting[LineOf(s)] - 1]
    /\ tokenAt' = RingNext(s)

Advance(s) ==
    /\ stage[s] = "washing"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "rinsing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, held, waiting, pool>>

Finish(s) ==
    /\ stage[s] = "rinsing"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "free"]
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {held[s]}
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, waiting>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Lines : Arrive(l)
    \/ \E s \in 1 .. Stations : PassToken(s)
    \/ \E s \in 1 .. Stations : Admit(s)
    \/ \E s \in 1 .. Stations : Advance(s)
    \/ \E s \in 1 .. Stations : Finish(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityInvariant ==
    /\ Cardinality(UsedBays) <= Cardinality(Bays)
    /\ pool \cap UsedBays = {}
    /\ pool \cup UsedBays = Bays
    /\ \A s, t \in Occupied : (s # t) => held[s] # held[t]

================================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Stations = 4
    Lines = {"L1", "L2"}
    Bays = {b1, b2}
    MaxWait = 2
INVARIANT CapacityInvariant
nl:
Two automated car-wash conveyor lines are installed side by side and, to save on plumbing, they draw wash bays from a single shared pool of water-recycling bays. The four wash stations are wired in a ring, and a single physical token circulates around that ring; only the station currently holding the token is allowed to pull a waiting car into a bay. Stations at odd positions belong to conveyor line one and stations at even positions belong to conveyor line two, so the two lines interleave on the same ring. When a car is admitted the station begins a wash, then advances to a rinse, and finally finishes and frees its bay back to the pool. Cars queue up as arrivals for each line before they can be admitted, and a token holder that has nothing to admit simply passes the token onward. Because both lines share the same finite pool, the design must guarantee that the combined number of bays in use across the two lines never climbs above the pool's physical capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state the number of wash stations that are not free never exceeds the shared pool's bay capacity.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od2m9p5t2 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Tasks, Ctrls, MaxEpoch

NONE == "none"
Unclaimed == [ctrl |-> NONE, ep |-> 0]

VARIABLES pool, claim, delivered, epoch
vars == <<pool, claim, delivered, epoch>>

Claimed == {t \in Tasks : claim[t].ctrl # NONE}

Init ==
    /\ pool = Tasks
    /\ claim = [t \in Tasks |-> Unclaimed]
    /\ delivered = {}
    /\ epoch = 0

Claim(c, t) ==
    /\ t \in pool
    /\ pool' = pool \ {t}
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![t] = [ctrl |-> c, ep |-> epoch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<delivered, epoch>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, claim, delivered>>

SweepStale(t) ==
    /\ claim[t].ctrl # NONE
    /\ claim[t].ep < epoch
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {t}
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![t] = Unclaimed]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<delivered, epoch>>

Deliver(t) ==
    /\ claim[t].ctrl # NONE
    /\ claim[t].ep = epoch
    /\ t \notin delivered
    /\ delivered' = delivered \cup {t}
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![t] = Unclaimed]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, epoch>>

Idle ==
    /\ delivered = Tasks
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls, t \in Tasks : Claim(c, t)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : SweepStale(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : Deliver(t)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Partition ==
    /\ pool \cap Claimed = {}
    /\ pool \cap delivered = {}
    /\ Claimed \cap delivered = {}
    /\ pool \cup Claimed \cup delivered = Tasks

================================================================================
nl:
A warehouse runs a fleet of picking robots that is driven by two independent dispatch controllers, and both controllers draw jobs from one shared pool of delivery tasks. Each task starts life in the shared pool; a controller may claim a task on behalf of the fleet, stamping the claim with the controller's identity and the current configuration epoch. From time to time the operations desk reconfigures the fleet, which bumps the global epoch by one, and any claim that was stamped with an older epoch becomes stale and must be swept back into the pool before it can be worked again. A robot only physically delivers a task whose claim is stamped with the current epoch, and delivery is a one-way, irreversible commitment: once a task has been delivered it is retired for good and must never re-enter the pool or be claimed or delivered a second time. Because two controllers share the pool and epochs keep changing, the design must ensure that every task lives in exactly one of the three states (pooled, claimed, or delivered) and that a delivered task is truly final.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No task is ever delivered more than once, because a delivered task can never simultaneously be pooled or claimed and never leaves the delivered state.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od5m4p3t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Slots, MaxPool

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES pool, slotOf, playerSlot
vars == <<pool, slotOf, playerSlot>>

Seated(p) == playerSlot[p] # NONE

Init ==
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ slotOf = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ playerSlot = [p \in Players |-> NONE]

Request(p) ==
    /\ p \notin pool
    /\ ~Seated(p)
    /\ Cardinality(pool) < MaxPool
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOf, playerSlot>>

Assign(p, s) ==
    /\ p \in pool
    /\ slotOf[s] = NONE
    /\ pool' = pool \ {p}
    /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![s] = p]
    /\ playerSlot' = [playerSlot EXCEPT ![p] = s]

Release(s) ==
    /\ slotOf[s] # NONE
    /\ playerSlot' = [playerSlot EXCEPT ![slotOf[s]] = NONE]
    /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED pool

Abandon(p) ==
    /\ p \in pool
    /\ pool' = pool \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOf, playerSlot>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players : Request(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots : Assign(p, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Release(s)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Abandon(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutualInverse ==
    /\ \A s \in Slots : slotOf[s] # NONE => playerSlot[slotOf[s]] = s
    /\ \A p \in Players : playerSlot[p] # NONE => slotOf[playerSlot[p]] = p

================================================================================
nl:
An online multiplayer game runs a matchmaker that seats waiting players into a small fixed set of game-session slots. Players who want a match first land in a bounded waiting pool, and because the pool applies backpressure, a new join request is refused whenever the pool is already at its maximum size. The matchmaker's internal request messages can be reordered in transit, so the matchmaker may pick any waiting player, not necessarily the one who asked first, and seat them into any currently empty slot. Seating records the pairing in two directions: the slot remembers which player it holds, and the player remembers which slot they occupy. When a session ends the slot is released and both directions of the pairing are cleared. A waiting player who gives up can also be dropped from the pool. The central correctness concern is that the two directional records stay mutually consistent so that a slot is never handed to two different players and a player never occupies two slots at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot-to-player and player-to-slot records are always mutual inverses, so no slot is double-allocated to two players and no player holds two slots.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od16m7p4t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Stations, Drugs, Stock, MaxQueue

NONE == "free"

VARIABLES reg, remaining, dispensed, phase, queue
vars == <<reg, remaining, dispensed, phase, queue>>

Init ==
    /\ reg = NONE
    /\ remaining = [d \in Drugs |-> Stock]
    /\ dispensed = [d \in Drugs |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [w \in Stations |-> "idle"]
    /\ queue = << >>

Prescribe(d) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < MaxQueue
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, d)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, remaining, dispensed, phase>>

Acquire(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = "idle"
    /\ reg = NONE
    /\ reg' = w
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "holding"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remaining, dispensed, queue>>

Dispense(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = "holding"
    /\ reg = w
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ LET d == Head(queue) IN
        /\ remaining[d] > 0
        /\ remaining' = [remaining EXCEPT ![d] = remaining[d] - 1]
        /\ dispensed' = [dispensed EXCEPT ![d] = dispensed[d] + 1]
        /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, phase>>

Release(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = "holding"
    /\ reg = w
    /\ reg' = NONE
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remaining, dispensed, queue>>

StaleSwap(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = "idle"
    /\ reg # NONE
    /\ reg # w
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

DropHead ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ remaining[Head(queue)] = 0
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, remaining, dispensed, phase>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drugs : Prescribe(d)
    \/ DropHead
    \/ \E w \in Stations : Acquire(w)
    \/ \E w \in Stations : Dispense(w)
    \/ \E w \in Stations : Release(w)
    \/ \E w \in Stations : StaleSwap(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BoundedStock ==
    \A d \in Drugs :
        /\ dispensed[d] <= Stock
        /\ remaining[d] >= 0
        /\ dispensed[d] + remaining[d] = Stock

================================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Stations = {w1, w2}
    Drugs = {d1, d2}
    Stock = 2
    MaxQueue = 3
INVARIANT BoundedStock
nl:
A hospital pharmacy has an automated narcotics cabinet whose single dispensing arm is guarded by a compare-and-swap control register. Several pharmacist workstations share the cabinet, and to take control of the arm a workstation performs a compare-and-swap: it succeeds only if the register currently reads "free", in which case the register is swapped to name that workstation. Some workstations are slow to respond but never actually fail, so a slow workstation may attempt a swap against a register value that has since changed; that swap simply fails and the workstation retries later without any effect. While a workstation holds the arm it may dispense pills one at a time, each dispense drawing a single unit from the bottle's remaining stock, and afterwards it swaps the register back to "free". The bottle began with a fixed number of pills, so at every moment the pills already dispensed plus the pills still remaining must add up to that original stock, and the number dispensed must never run past it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The count of pills dispensed never exceeds the bottle's original stock, and dispensed plus remaining always equals that fixed original amount.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od14m6p1t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Drones, MaxVer, MaxClock, LeaseLen

NONE == "none"
NoSnap == 99

VARIABLES clock, ver, lease, snap, chain
vars == <<clock, ver, lease, snap, chain>>

LeaseValid(dr) == lease.owner = dr /\ lease.exp > clock

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ lease = [owner |-> NONE, exp |-> 0]
    /\ snap = [dr \in Drones |-> NoSnap]
    /\ chain = << >>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, lease, snap, chain>>

AcquireLease(dr) ==
    /\ lease.exp <= clock
    /\ lease' = [owner |-> dr, exp |-> clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, ver, snap, chain>>

Snapshot(dr) ==
    /\ LeaseValid(dr)
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![dr] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, ver, lease, chain>>

Commit(dr) ==
    /\ LeaseValid(dr)
    /\ snap[dr] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ chain' = Append(chain, ver)
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![dr] = NoSnap]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease>>

AdminForce ==
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ chain' = Append(chain, ver)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, snap>>

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E dr \in Drones : AcquireLease(dr)
    \/ \E dr \in Drones : Snapshot(dr)
    \/ \E dr \in Drones : Commit(dr)
    \/ AdminForce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
    /\ Len(chain) = ver
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(chain) : chain[i] = i - 1

================================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {r1, r2}
    MaxVer = 3
    MaxClock = 3
    LeaseLen = 2
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A swarm of autonomous drones surveils an active wildfire and maintains a single shared incident record describing the current fire front. To write to that record a drone must first hold a time-limited lease, granted only when no valid lease is outstanding and stamped with an expiry deadline measured against a shared mission clock; once the clock passes the deadline the lease is considered expired and may be re-granted. To prevent lost updates, a drone takes a snapshot of the record's version before it writes and is allowed to commit its update only if the version has not changed since that snapshot, which guarantees its write was based on the very latest data. Each successful commit advances the version by one and appends, to the audit chain, the base version the writer had observed. A privileged incident commander can override the lease mechanism and force an update at any time, but even a forced update is based on the current version. Correctness requires that the audit chain shows every update built directly on its immediate predecessor, so no writer's changes were silently lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed update in the audit chain was based on the immediately preceding version, so no update ever overwrote and lost a concurrent commit.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od2m0p0t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, MaxVer

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES owner, ver, inCS, read, attempts
vars == <<owner, ver, inCS, read, attempts>>

Init ==
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ inCS = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]
    /\ read = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ attempts = {}

Read(r) ==
    /\ ~inCS[r]
    /\ read' = [read EXCEPT ![r] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, inCS, attempts>>

Try(r) ==
    /\ ~inCS[r]
    /\ attempts' = attempts \cup {[by |-> r, exp |-> read[r]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, inCS, read>>

ApplyOk(m) ==
    /\ m \in attempts
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ ver = m.exp
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = m.by
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![m.by] = TRUE]
    /\ attempts' = attempts \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED read

ApplyFail(m) ==
    /\ m \in attempts
    /\ (owner # NONE \/ ver # m.exp)
    /\ attempts' = attempts \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, inCS, read>>

Release(r) ==
    /\ inCS[r]
    /\ owner = r
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<read, attempts>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Read(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Try(r)
    \/ \E m \in attempts : ApplyOk(m)
    \/ \E m \in attempts : ApplyFail(m)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Release(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutexConsistent ==
    \A r \in Robots : inCS[r] <=> (owner = r)

================================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2}
    MaxVer = 4
INVARIANT MutexConsistent
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a single narrow recharging alcove that only one robot may physically occupy at a time. Access is arbitrated by an optimistic lock: a shared register carries the current holder and a version number. A robot that wants the alcove first reads the register's version, then submits an acquire attempt tagged with the version it saw. Because these attempts flow through the fleet's messaging fabric they may be delivered out of order, so attempts are applied in an arbitrary sequence. An attempt succeeds only if, at the moment it is applied, the alcove is unheld and the register version still matches the version the robot had read; on success the robot enters the alcove, the register names it as holder, and the version is bumped. An attempt whose version is stale or that finds the alcove held simply fails, and the robot must re-read and retry. When a robot leaves it clears the holder and bumps the version again. The essential requirement is that a robot is recorded as inside the alcove exactly when the register names it as the holder.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At all times a robot is inside the recharging alcove if and only if the shared register names it as the current holder, so two robots never occupy the alcove together.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od13m3p1t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Machines, MaxTerm, MaxVer

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES leader, term, up, ver, chain
vars == <<leader, term, up, ver, chain>>

Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ term = 0
    /\ up = [m \in Machines |-> TRUE]
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ chain = << >>

Elect(m) ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ up[m]
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = m
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<up, ver, chain>>

FailOver(m) ==
    /\ leader = m
    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, ver, chain>>

Recover(m) ==
    /\ ~up[m]
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, ver, chain>>

Apply(m) ==
    /\ leader = m
    /\ up[m]
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ chain' = Append(chain, ver)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, up>>

AdminForce ==
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ chain' = Append(chain, ver)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, up>>

Idle ==
    /\ ver = MaxVer
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ Idle
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Elect(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : FailOver(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Recover(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Apply(m)
    \/ AdminForce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ContiguousChain ==
    /\ (chain # << >> => chain[1] = 0)
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(chain) - 1 : chain[i + 1] = chain[i] + 1
    /\ Len(chain) = ver

================================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2, m3}
    MaxTerm = 3
    MaxVer = 3
INVARIANT ContiguousChain
nl:
A regional network of smart vending machines keeps a shared pricing record that only a single elected coordinator machine is allowed to update. The machines run a leader election: when there is no active leader, any machine that is powered up may win election and take office, which advances a monotonic term number. The sitting leader can fail over at any time, going offline and vacating the leadership so that a survivor can be elected under a fresh, higher term. While in office and online, the leader applies pricing updates, and each applied update advances the record's version by one and appends to the change chain the version it was built upon. A regional administrator can also override the whole scheme and force a pricing update directly, but such a forced update likewise builds on the record's current version. Because leadership changes hands on failure and terms only ever move forward, the operators need a guarantee that no pricing update was ever lost: the change chain must always be an unbroken run in which each update was based on exactly the version that came right before it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The pricing change chain is always contiguous, with every update based on exactly its immediate predecessor version, so no committed pricing update was ever overwritten and lost.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od19m6p1t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Patrons, Books, MaxVer, MaxClock, LeaseLen

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES clock, bookVer, lease, inflight, chain
vars == <<clock, bookVer, lease, inflight, chain>>

LeaseValid(p, b) == lease[b].owner = p /\ lease[b].exp > clock

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ bookVer = [b \in Books |-> 0]
    /\ lease = [b \in Books |-> [owner |-> NONE, exp |-> 0]]
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ chain = [b \in Books |-> << >>]

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookVer, lease, inflight, chain>>

AcquireLease(p, b) ==
    /\ lease[b].exp <= clock
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![b] = [owner |-> p, exp |-> clock + LeaseLen]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, bookVer, inflight, chain>>

Submit(p, b) ==
    /\ LeaseValid(p, b)
    /\ bookVer[b] < MaxVer
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {[book |-> b, base |-> bookVer[b], by |-> p]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, bookVer, lease, chain>>

ApplyValid(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflight
    /\ bookVer[m.book] = m.base
    /\ bookVer[m.book] < MaxVer
    /\ bookVer' = [bookVer EXCEPT ![m.book] = bookVer[m.book] + 1]
    /\ chain' = [chain EXCEPT ![m.book] = Append(chain[m.book], m.base)]
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease>>

ApplyStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflight
    /\ bookVer[m.book] # m.base
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, bookVer, lease, chain>>

Idle ==
    /\ clock = MaxClock
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ Idle
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : AcquireLease(p, b)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : Submit(p, b)
    \/ \E m \in inflight : ApplyValid(m)
    \/ \E m \in inflight : ApplyStale(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
    \A b \in Books :
        /\ Len(chain[b]) = bookVer[b]
        /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(chain[b]) : chain[b][i] = i - 1

================================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Patrons = {p1, p2}
    Books = {bk1, bk2}
    MaxVer = 2
    MaxClock = 2
    LeaseLen = 2
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A city library runs an online reservation system for its most-requested titles. Each book has a reservation record with a version counter, and to change a book's record a patron must hold a short lease on that book, granted only when the book's current lease is free or has expired against the shared system clock. Because confirmation messages travel through a distributed queue, they can be delivered out of order: when a patron with a valid lease acts, the system snapshots the book's current version into an in-flight reservation message, and those messages may later be applied in any order. A reservation message is only applied if the book's version still equals the version the message captured; if some other message advanced that book's version first, the late message is stale and is dropped rather than applied, which is exactly how the system avoids losing an update. Every applied message advances that book's version by one and records, in the book's audit chain, the base version it built upon. The system must guarantee that each book's audit chain is an unbroken succession where every update was based on the version immediately before it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every book, each recorded update was based on the immediately preceding version, so no reservation update was ever silently lost to a stale write.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od18m5p2t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Total, Quorum

VARIABLES available, reserved, consumed, proposing, votes
vars == <<available, reserved, consumed, proposing, votes>>

Init ==
    /\ available = Total
    /\ reserved = 0
    /\ consumed = 0
    /\ proposing = FALSE
    /\ votes = {}

Propose ==
    /\ ~proposing
    /\ available > 0
    /\ available' = available - 1
    /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
    /\ proposing' = TRUE
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED consumed

Vote(n) ==
    /\ proposing
    /\ n \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<available, reserved, consumed, proposing>>

Commit ==
    /\ proposing
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ consumed' = consumed + 1
    /\ proposing' = FALSE
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED available

Abort ==
    /\ proposing
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ available' = available + 1
    /\ proposing' = FALSE
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED consumed

AdminForce ==
    /\ proposing

The pool of tokens is conserved: a token is always in exactly one of three places, available in the pool, reserved while a vote is in progress, or consumed after an approved unlock. If a proposal cannot gather a quorum it is aborted and its reserved token returns to the available pool.     /\ fine = [b \in Blocks |-> NONE]
    /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ cap = [b \in Blocks |-> 1]

AcquireCoarse(cr, b) ==
    /\ coarse[b] = NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![b] = cr]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, occ, cap>>

AcquireFine(cr, b) ==
    /\ coarse[b] = cr
    /\ fine[b] = NONE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = cr]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, occ, cap>>

Place(cr, b) ==
    /\ coarse[b] = cr
    /\ fine[b] = cr
    /\ occ[b] < cap[b]
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = occ[b] + 1]
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, cap>>

Remove(cr, b) ==
    /\ coarse[b] = cr
    /\ occ[b] > 0
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = occ[b] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, cap>>

ReleaseCoarse(cr, b) ==
    /\ coarse[b] = cr
    /\ fine[b] = NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, occ, cap>>

RaiseCap(b) ==
    /\ cap[b] < MaxCap
    /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![b] = cap[b] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, occ>>

LowerCap(b) ==
    /\ cap[b] > occ[b]
    /\ cap[b] > 0
    /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![b] = cap[b] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, occ>>

    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, b \in Blocks : AcquireCoarse(cr, b)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, b \in Blocks : AcquireFine(cr, b)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, b \in Blocks : Place(cr, b)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, b \in Blocks : Remove(cr, b)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, b \in Blocks : ReleaseCoarse(cr, b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : RaiseCap(b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : LowerCap(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinCapacity ==
    \A b \in Blocks : occ[b] <= cap[b]

nl:
A container-ship crane yard is divided into storage blocks, each holding a limited number of containers. Cranes stack and unstack containers, and to work a block a crane must take locks hierarchically: first a coarse lock on the whole block, then a fine lock on a working position inside it. Only the crane holding both the coarse lock and the fine lock on a block may place a container there, and placing is refused if the block is already at its capacity. After placing a container the crane releases the fine lock but may keep the coarse lock to place again. A crane may also remove a container from a block it coarse-holds, and it releases the coarse lock when done. The yard supervisor can change a block's capacity at runtime, raising it freely up to an equipment maximum, but only lowering a block's capacity when there is slack, that is, when the block's current capacity strictly exceeds the number of containers currently in it. The invariant the yard must preserve is that no block ever holds more containers than its current, possibly just-changed, capacity allows.
SAFETY PROPERTY: In every reachable state the number of containers stored in each block never exceeds that block's current capacity.

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker assigns donated blood units to refrigerated storage slots. Each unit may occupy at most one slot and each slot may hold at most one unit, and the assignment is recorded in both directions so the two records must stay mutually consistent. The bank operates under configuration epochs: an epoch-numbered reconfiguration of the cold room bumps the epoch and clears every current slot assignment so the inventory can be re-stocked from scratch under the new layout. The set of storage slots that are actually in service can also change at runtime as refrigerators are switched on or off, so the number of usable slots grows and shrinks; a slot may only be taken out of service when it is empty. A unit can be assigned only to a slot that is currently in service and free, and a stored unit can be withdrawn, which frees its slot. The tracker must guarantee that its two directional records never disagree, so no slot is ever double-booked to two units and no unit is ever recorded in two slots.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot-to-unit and unit-to-slot records are always mutual inverses, so no storage slot is double-allocated and no blood unit is placed in two slots.

    /\ term = 0
    /\ up = [m \in Machines |-> TRUE]

    /\ leader' = m

    /\ leader = m
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderHist, posted>>

    /\ ~up[m]
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, leaderHist, posted>>

    /\ up[m]
    /\ [poster |-> m, term |-> term] \notin posted
    /\ posted' = posted \cup {[poster |-> m, term |-> term]}

    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    MaxTerm = 3
INVARIANT NoUnauthorized
nl:
A consortium of banks runs an interbank settlement batch that is coordinated by a single elected leader machine. Leadership is term-numbered: whenever there is no active leader, any live machine can win election and take office, which advances a monotonically increasing term and records, for that term, which machine holds office. The current leader, while it is up, may post settlement entries into the batch, and each posted entry is stamped with the poster's identity and the term under which it was posted. One of the machines can crash silently: a leader that crashes goes offline and immediately vacates its office so that a survivor may be elected under a fresh term. A crashed machine can later recover and rejoin. The regulator's absolute requirement is that no settlement entry was ever posted by an unauthorized or stale participant: every entry in the batch must have been posted by exactly the machine that legitimately held office for that entry's term.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every posted settlement entry was posted by the machine that was the recorded, authorized office-holder for that entry's term, so no unauthorized or stale participant ever posted.

vars == <<clock, stage, lease, certified>>

    /\ stage = [c \in Cars |-> "waiting"]
    /\ lease = [c \in Cars |-> [owner |-> NONE, exp |-> 0]]

Tick ==

    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, lease, certified>>

    /\ lease[c].exp <= clock

    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, stage, certified>>

BeginWash(ctl, c) ==

    /\ LeaseValid(ctl, c)
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "washing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, certified>>

    /\ LeaseValid(ctl, c)
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "clean"]
    /\ certified' = certified \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease>>

    /\ stage[c] # "clean"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "clean"]
    /\ certified' = certified \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease>>

Idle ==
    /\ clock = MaxClock
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ Tick
    \/ \E ctl \in Controllers, c \in Cars : GrantLease(ctl, c)
    \/ \E ctl \in Controllers, c \in Cars : BeginWash(ctl, c)
    \/ \E ctl \in Controllers, c \in Cars : Certify(ctl, c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : AdminForce(c)
    \/ Idle

    Controllers = {ct1, ct2}
    MaxClock = 3
    LeaseLen = 2

nl:
An automated car-wash conveyor line certifies each car as finished exactly once. A wash controller must hold a time-limited lease on the wash tunnel for a particular car before it may advance that car through its stages, and the lease is granted against a shared clock and expires when the clock passes its deadline. A car moves from waiting, to being washed under a valid lease, and finally to certified-clean, which is a final sink state: once a car is certified it can never move back to an earlier stage and can never be certified a second time. Certification normally requires the controller to hold a currently valid lease for that car, but a site administrator can override the lease requirement and force-certify a car directly. Whether certification happens through a valid lease or through an administrator override, it is a one-way, irreversible event. The line must guarantee that the set of certified cars is exactly the set of cars sitting in the certified-clean stage, which together with the sink property means each car is certified at most once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A car is in the recorded certified set if and only if it is in the certified-clean stage, and the certified-clean stage is a sink, so no car is ever certified more than once.

    /\ queue = [z \in {"A", "B"} |-> << >>]

    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![t] = "queued"]
    /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![Zone(t)] = Append(queue[Zone(t)], t)]

    /\ queue[Zone(t)] # << >>
    /\ Head(queue[Zone(t)]) = t
    /\ \E b \in free :

        /\ onblock' = [onblock EXCEPT ![t] = b]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![t] = "run"]
    /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![Zone(t)] = Tail(queue[Zone(t)])]

    /\ free' = free \cup {onblock[t]}

nl:
A subway signalling system controls two lines that, at an interchange, share one common pool of physical track blocks. Each line has its own bounded boarding queue where trains wait for entry, and the queue applies backpressure: a train cannot join a line's queue once that queue is already at its maximum length. A waiting train at the head of its line's queue may be admitted onto the track only if a block is free in the shared pool, at which point it claims that block and leaves the queue. A running train may advance by swapping onto a different currently free block, releasing the block it was on. When a train exits the network it releases its block back to the shared pool. Because both lines draw blocks from the same pool, the signalling logic must guarantee that the blocks are conserved and never double-occupied: every block is either free or held by exactly one running train, and the number of running trains can never exceed the number of blocks in the pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state each track block is either free or occupied by exactly one running train, and the count of running trains never exceeds the shared pool's number of blocks.

    /\ holder = 1
    /\ using = [s \in 1 .. Stations |-> FALSE]

    /\ done = 0

    /\ backlog' = backlog + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, using, done>>

    /\ ~using[s]
    /\ using' = [using EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]

    /\ backlog > 0
    /\ done < MaxDone
    /\ backlog' = backlog - 1

    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, backlog, done>>

    /\ ~using[s]
    /\ holder' = RingNext(s)

    /\ holder' = s

    MaxBacklog = 2
    MaxDone = 2

A print shop has one high-volume printer shared by several operator stations wired into a token ring. A single token circulates around the ring, and only the station currently holding the token is permitted to seize the printer and run a job on it. Jobs are submitted into a bounded backlog; a station that holds the token and finds the printer idle may begin using it, print jobs off the backlog one at a time while it holds the printer, and then must stop using the printer before it passes the token on to the next station in the ring. The shop's manager has a privileged override that can hand the token directly to any chosen station regardless of the ring order, for example to rush a priority job.     /\ ver' = ver + 1

    MaxVer = 4

nl:
A pharmacy's automated dispenser is shared by several workstations that coordinate through an optimistic lock rather than a hard mutex. A shared control record carries a holder field and a version number. A workstation that wants the dispenser first reads the current version, then tries to acquire: the acquire succeeds only if the dispenser is unheld and the version still equals what the workstation had read, and on success the version is bumped and the workstation becomes the holder. If the version has moved on, the acquire fails and the workstation must re-read and retry. While holding the dispenser a workstation dispenses pills one at a time, each drawing one unit from the bottle's remaining stock, and then releases, bumping the version again. A supervising pharmacist has an administrative override that can dispense a pill directly without going through the lock at all. The bottle started with a fixed stock, so the design must ensure that the number of pills dispensed and the number remaining always add back to that original stock and the dispensed count never overruns it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The pills dispensed plus the pills remaining always equal the bottle's fixed original stock, and the dispensed count never exceeds it.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Routes, Coords, Participants

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES phase, coord, votes, committed
vars == <<phase, coord, votes, committed>>

Init ==
    /\ phase = [r \in Routes |-> "idle"]
    /\ coord = [r \in Routes |-> NONE]
    /\ votes = [r \in Routes |-> {}]
    /\ committed = {}

Propose(co, r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "prepared"]
    /\ coord' = [coord EXCEPT ![r] = co]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![r] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED committed

CastVote(p, r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "prepared"
    /\ p \notin votes[r]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![r] = votes[r] \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, coord, committed>>

Commit(r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "prepared"
    /\ votes[r] = Participants
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "committed"]
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, votes>>

Abort(r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "prepared"
    /\ votes[r] # Participants
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ coord' = [coord EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![r] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED committed

Idle ==
    /\ \A r \in Routes : phase[r] = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E co \in Coords, r \in Routes : Propose(co, r)
    \/ \E p \in Participants, r \in Routes : CastVote(p, r)
    \/ \E r \in Routes : Commit(r)
    \/ \E r \in Routes : Abort(r)
    \/ Idle

CommitOnce ==
    \A r \in Routes : (r \in committed) <=> (phase[r] = "committed")

nl:
A subway signalling network reserves end-to-end routes using a two-phase commit run by route coordinators, and two independent coordinators draw from one shared pool of candidate routes. A route begins idle. A coordinator may propose a route, moving it into the prepared phase and taking ownership of the round. The signalling participants along the route then cast yes-votes for a prepared route. Once every participant has voted yes, the coordinator commits the route, which is an irreversible physical action: switches are thrown and the route becomes committed for good and can never be committed again or rolled back. A prepared route that does not gather all votes can instead be aborted, returning it to idle so it can be retried later, possibly by the other coordinator. Because two coordinators share the same pool of routes and the commit action is irreversible, the network must guarantee that the recorded set of committed routes is exactly the set of routes standing in the committed phase, and that committing is a one-way door.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A route is in the committed set if and only if it is in the committed phase, and no committed route ever leaves that phase, so each route is committed at most once.

    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, bagChute, chuteBag>>

    /\ chuteBag[m.chute] = NONE
    /\ bagChute[m.bag] = NONE

    \/ \E n \in Nodes : FailOver(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, b \in Bags, c \in Chutes : Issue(n, b, c)

An airport baggage router assigns bags to delivery chutes, and only a single elected leader node is allowed to make assignments. The nodes run a leader election: when there is no leader, any node that is online may take leadership. The elected leader issues assignment requests, but because these requests travel through the router's messaging fabric they can be delivered out of order, so pending assignment messages are applied in an arbitrary sequence. An assignment message is applied only if, at that moment, both the target chute is still empty and the named bag is still unassigned; otherwise the message is stale and is dropped. SAFETY PROPERTY: The bag-to-chute and chute-to-bag records are always mutual inverses, so no chute is double-allocated to two bags and no bag occupies two chutes.

    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease>>

    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![j] = [owner |-> NONE, exp |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, jobVer, applied>>

    /\ \A j \in Jobs : jobVer[j] = MaxVer
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E sp \in Spoolers, j \in Jobs : GrantLease(sp, j)
    \/ \E sp \in Spoolers, j \in Jobs : ApplyEdit(sp, j)
    \/ \E sp \in Spoolers, j \in Jobs : ReleaseLease(sp, j)

nl:
A print shop runs two independent spooler instances that share one common pool of print-job records, each job carrying its own version counter. To edit a job's record a spooler must hold a lease on that specific job; a lease is granted only when the job's current lease is free or has expired against the shared clock, and it names the holding spooler and an expiry deadline. Because the lease is exclusive per job, only one spooler at a time can be editing any given job, which is how concurrent edits are serialized and lost updates are prevented. When a lease-holding spooler applies an edit it stamps the edit with the job's current version as its base and advances that job's version by one; every applied edit is recorded in a global set of applied edits tagged by job and base version. The shared clock ticks forward, expiring old leases. The shop's correctness requirement is that, for every job, the set of base versions that were actually applied forms a complete, gap-free run from zero up to just below the job's current version, so no edit was ever lost or duplicated.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For each print job the recorded applied base versions are exactly the contiguous set from zero up to one below the job's current version, so no edit was lost or applied twice.
